title: Cian
extract: In Irish mythology, Cian or Cían (Irish pronunciation:[ciənˠ]), nicknamed Scal Balb, was the son of Dian Cecht, the physician of the Tuatha Dé Danann, and is best known as the father of Lugh Lámhfhada (Lugh of the Long Arm). Cían's brothers were Cu, Cethen, and Miach. Cían was slain by the Sons of Tuireann, for which Lugh demanded various treasures from around the world as éraic (compensation), according to the account in the Book of Invasions (Lebor Gabála Érenn, LGE) as well as the late romance version The Fate of the Children of Tuireann. Cian means 'enduring one'; cían signifying 'long, enduring, far, distant'. Scal Balb is a nickname borne by other personages and means 'dumb champion', with 'dumb' in the archaic sense of 'unable to make speech'. By most accounts, Lug's mother is the Fomorian princess Ethniu (daughter of Balor of the Evil Eye).
